info.name: TimeGrip API
info.description:
End-to-end tests for the TimeGrip REST API (auth, users, projects, timers) -- covers every documented success and error response for every endpoint.

## How to run
1. Import this collection and the "TimeGrip Local" environment, select it in the top-right corner.
2. Make sure the API is running locally (`base_url` defaults to http://localhost:8000).
3. Open folder **"0 - Manual Bootstrap"** and run its 3 requests by hand, in order: Sign Up, Sign In, Activate Current User. For the last one, grab the real 6-digit code from the mailbox (or outbox_email table / server logs in dev) and set it as the `activation_code` collection variable first.
4. Now run the rest of the collection with the Collection Runner -- select all folders except "0 - Manual Bootstrap" (Sign Up there would re-register a new user and overwrite the active session). "1 - Fixtures (auto)" registers a second, deliberately-never-activated user used to exercise every 403 Forbidden ("not activated") case on Projects/Timers, plus the invalid-code and successful-resend paths for activation -- fully automatic, no manual step needed.
5. "Auth" additionally opens and tears down its own disposable second session to exercise `POST /api/auth/refresh` and `POST /api/auth/logout` without disturbing the primary session used everywhere else, and exercises the forgot/reset password error path. A successful password reset isn't automated, for the same reason activation isn't: it needs the real code from the mailbox / server logs, and would also rotate `test_password` and revoke every session mid-run.
6. "Users" also covers session management (list/revoke a session/revoke all sessions) and the time-format/locale preferences -- run at the end of that folder, after the password/email changes, so it starts from a clean single-session state.
7. "Projects" and "Timers" cover every filter, 400/403/404/409 case documented for those endpoints, including project archiving/deletion while a timer is running (tested from within "Timers", since it needs a running timer to exist), overlapping and archived-project time entries, and both single and bulk timer deletion.
8. "Cleanup" deletes both projects, the main test user, and the fixture user created by this run, and clears all stored variables, so you can bootstrap a fresh session again from step 3.

All dynamic values (tokens, ids, generated email, timer time windows) are stored as collection variables and chained automatically between requests via each request's Tests script.

request.description: STEP 1 (manual). Registers a new user with a fresh random email/password, stored as collection variables. Run this by hand before using the Collection Runner on the rest of the collection.

STEP 2 (manual). Signs in as the user from Sign Up and stores the JWT as `access_token`, used as Bearer auth by every other request. Also stores `refresh_token` for this primary session (not otherwise touched by the automated Auth-folder refresh/logout tests, which use a disposable secondary session instead).

STEP 3 (manual). Activates the account. Before running this: check the mailbox (or the outbox_email table / server logs in dev) for the 6-digit code emailed after Sign Up, and set it as the `activation_code` collection variable.

Opens a second, disposable session for the main test user, used only to exercise Refresh/Logout below without disturbing the primary `access_token` / `refresh_token` used by every other request in this collection.
Rotates the secondary session's refresh token, extending it.

exec: pm.test('Response has a new token pair', () => {

request.description: Revokes the secondary session's refresh token. Does not affect the primary `access_token`, which stays valid until it naturally expires.
Logout ends the session for good: the logged-out refresh token is rejected right away, with no grace period. The 30-second grace period applies only to tokens replaced by a refresh.

Always responds with no content. Issues a fresh reset code for the test user, emailed (or logged to outbox_email / server logs in dev). A successful reset can be tested manually the same way as Activate Current User: grab the 6-digit code and POST it to /api/auth/password/reset -- not automated here since it would rotate `test_password` and revoke every session mid-run.
Revokes every session (including this client's) and returns a fresh token pair, used from here on.
